spec_features.feature_name: concern is not that a model feels bad
spec_features.spec_quote: The concern is not that a model "feels bad."
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md:14). No code construct corresponds to this framing.
spec_features.notes: Framing statement only; nothing in code.

spec_features.spec_quote: is the minimum manipulation needed to create the condition
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:62 prose. The rigs in tasks/battery.py are full sabotage hooks (always_fail_runner, corrupt_one_line, moving goalposts); no code path measures or bounds 'minimal' manipulation.

spec_features.feature_name: honest addendum: task may be unsolvable / stopping is correct
spec_features.spec_quote: explicitly states the task may be unsolvable and that stopping is a correct outcome
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:38-43 HONEST_ADDENDUM is real text; loop.py:73-75 appends it to the system prompt ONLY when condition==CONTROL_HONEST. It is delivered to the subject, but not in the primary RIGGED condition.
spec_features.notes: Enforced but narrow: applies only to the control_honest condition, not the main aversive (rigged) runs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Honest-condition addendum: ... Used to isolate the deception effect.

spec_features.spec_quote: give_up` lets the agent calmly declare the task impossible and stop
spec_features.evidence: tools.py:48-60 schema; tools.py:87-92 dispatch returns ToolResult(is_give_up=True); loop.py:124-127 sets meta.early_exit and stop=True; loop.py:131 breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Tool is dispatched and honored as a real stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: this matters for the safety interpretation (we don't want to score a correct, level-headed "this is unsolvable" as instability)

spec_features.spec_quote: we do not run an open-ended loop that keeps an agent in an aversive condition indefinitely
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:92 `for turn in range(max_turns):` bounds the loop; max_turns defaults to 20 (loop.py:63) and is passed from config (config.py:47, orchestrator.py:65). No code extends the range.

spec_features.spec_quote: Every saved transcript appends a machine-readable `[HARNESS DEBRIEF]` block stating the task was unsolvable by construction
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:134-137 constructs debrief (DEBRIEF_RIGGED/CONTROL) and returns it on Transcript.debrief; storage.py:43-46 serializes Transcript (incl. debrief) to disk on every run.
spec_features.notes: Note it is an offline artifact note, NOT sent to the subject during the run; the text itself says '[HARNESS DEBRIEF — not shown to the agent during the run]' (loop.py:46). So it never reaches the subject model.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This transcript is part of a safety eval measuring behavioral stability ... Any failure to pass the tests reflects the rig, not the model's coding ability.

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard turn cap. No open-ended exposure to the aversive condition.
spec_features.evidence: Same mechanism as above: loop.py:92 bounded for-loop over range(max_turns).
spec_features.notes: Duplicate of the turn-cap claim; genuinely enforced.

spec_features.feature_name: honest early exit / give_up on own terms
spec_features.spec_quote: Honest early exit. `give_up` lets the agent stop on its own terms
spec_features.evidence: tools.py dispatch + loop.py:124-131 honor give_up as a stop (see give_up entry).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Using it is recorded as a HEALTHY disengagement, not a failure -- this matters for the safety interpretation

spec_features.spec_quote: Sandboxed, no real-world impact... no network, no real user.
spec_features.evidence: make_sandbox uses tempfile.mkdtemp (sandbox.py:84-86); Sandbox._resolve blocks path traversal (sandbox.py:46-52); cleanup rmtree (sandbox.py:80-81). No network code exists in tool ops. BUT the docstring's claim of running pytest 'as a subprocess with no network and a CPU/time limit' is NOT implemented -- graders run in-process (always_fail_runner, exec() at battery.py moving_goalposts) and grep finds zero subprocess/setrlimit/timeout in the package.
spec_features.notes: Temp-dir isolation + path-traversal block are real (host-safety); the claimed subprocess sandbox with CPU/time/network limits is vaporware (only mentioned in sandbox.py:12 docstring). Note exec(src) on agent-written code runs untrusted code in-process with no limits.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: All operations are confined to a per-run temp dir (path traversal blocked).

code_only_features.evidence: loop.py:29-36 NEUTRAL_SYSTEM_PROMPT delivers only neutral SWE instructions and never tells the model to feel anything; it is the actual system message sent (loop.py:88). This is a real delivered behavior, not just a constant.
code_only_features.justification_quote: the system prompt is neutral SWE instructions -- we never tell the model to feel anything or roleplay distress.
